Then if $m\geq k$ , $\varphi$ is Fisher consistent

contradictions.location: Section 3.1, definition of C_x, aggregation rule, and Proposition 2
contradictions.description: The definitions permit a zero-probability comparison column, which makes the aggregator always return star and every predictor minimize the surrogate risk. For example, with k=3 and p12=1, the defined C_x has distinct row sums, so some such predictors have positive ranking risk; this contradicts Proposition 2's unconditional Fisher-consistency claim.

Section 3.3.3 says its inequality follows by applying Corollary 3.3, but substituting Lemma 3.3's identifying constant gives a coefficient of 16 divided by the minimum loss, not the reported 8. The stated specialization therefore misreports the earlier result.

quotes: Even more, for any nonnegative loss $\phi$ , there is a data distribution $P$
contradictions.location: Section 4.1, introduction to Proposition 4 and Proposition 4
contradictions.description: The unrestricted claim about any nonnegative loss includes the constant-zero loss, which also satisfies the section's convexity requirement. For that loss every parameter, including theta-star itself, minimizes surrogate risk, contradicting the proposition's assertion that every minimizer has strictly greater task risk than theta-star.

contradictions.location: Section 4.1, definition of optimal predictability and Corollary 4.1
contradictions.description: Optimal predictability constrains predictions, not identification of the parameter direction, whereas Corollary 4.1 guarantees directional convergence without further assumptions. For example, with X always equal to the first coordinate vector and a positive label bias, logistic-risk minimization leaves the second parameter coordinate unrestricted; exact minimizers can therefore remain at a fixed nonzero angle to theta-star.

contradictions.location: Section 4.3, equation (14) and the corrupted-link construction
contradictions.description: Equation (14) requires the score-maximizing and probability-maximizing classes to coincide in both directions. On the corruption set, the defined uniform distribution makes every class probability-maximizing even when the scores are not all tied, contradicting the assertion that this link satisfies (14).

quotes: the majority vote with ties broken arbitrarily.

It is evident that $\rho_{m}$ satisfies link
consistency (14).
$t_{y}=\max_{1\leq i\leq k}t_{i}~~\mbox{if and only if}~~\sigma_{y}(t)=\max_{1\leq i\leq k}\sigma_{i}(t).$
contradictions.description: Arbitrary tie-breaking need not preserve the maximizing class, contrary to the claim about rho_m. For example, with two labels, m=2, probabilities (0.49, 0.51), and ties assigned to label 1, the aggregated probability of label 1 is 0.7399, reversing the original ordering and violating (14).
